column1: # hot-race-costs.tsv — DECLARED SCHEDULING INPUTS for the partition in scripts/race-hot-tests.sh.
# Format: <entry point><TAB><milliseconds>. Comments start with '#'. Blank lines ignored.
# WHAT THESE NUMBERS ARE, AND WHAT THEY ARE NOT.
# They are the per-test durations Go itself reported on ONE developer container on
# 16 visible CPUs, GOMAXPROCS=4, SQLite, no Postgres service, whole selection 343.6s,
# exit 0. Every number below comes from the verbose log of that one
# The SAME selection exceeded 900s on ci-runner-8. So a number here is NOT a prediction of
# remote wall time, NOT evidence about any runner, and NOT a performance claim. It is a
# RELATIVE ORDERING used to divide the work deterministically. What a partition costs in CI
# is a CI measurement, and `check-test-timeout-headroom.sh` is what reports it.
# An entry NOT named here is still owned, at the helper's DEFAULT_COST_MS. Ownership never
# depends on this file. The opposite direction fails closed: a row naming an entry the live
# manifest no longer has is STALE and the helper exits 1, because a stale row silently
# unbalances every partition and nothing else would report it.
# A duration Go printed as 0.00s is recorded as 1 ms, not 0: it means 'under ten
# milliseconds', not 'free', and the helper refuses a non-positive cost so that a zero can
# To refresh: each CI partition runs with `-v`, so its log carries the durations measured on
# the machine that actually pays for them.
